generation.hypothesis: Spark plasma sintering (SPS) reduces the effective sintering temperature of powder metallurgy‐processed high-entropy alloys compared to conventional sintering methods.
generation.material_initial_state: Inert gas atomized or mechanically alloyed high-entropy alloy powders with preliminary loose packing or low-density compacts.
generation.intervention: Application of spark plasma sintering with rapid heating and plasma discharge under controlled inert atmosphere conditions.
generation.conditions: Experiments conducted under low-temperature regimes and rapid heating conditions (typical of SPS) as opposed to traditional high-temperature, slower heating sintering techniques.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced mass transport and accelerated diffusion at particle interfaces due to localized plasma effects and rapid heating, leading to effective densification.
generation.mechanism: The plasma discharges and rapid heating in SPS facilitate faster diffusion and sintering kinetics, lowering the activation energy needed for densification and reducing the overall temperature required for sintering.
generation.predicted_outcome: Densified high-entropy alloy samples with comparable or improved microstructural characteristics (e.g., fine grain structure) achieved at a sintering temperature significantly lower than that required by conventional sintering methods.
generation.baseline: Conventional sintering methods that require prolonged high-temperature treatments to achieve similar levels of densification.
generation.boundary: This effect is expected to hold true for powder metallurgically processed high-entropy alloys under inert or vacuum conditions; results may vary with different alloy compositions, powder characteristics, or processing atmospheres.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of the sintering temperature reduction is uncertain and will depend on factors such as powder particle size, alloy composition, and specific SPS parameters.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of equivalent high-entropy alloy powder compacts. Sinter one set using conventional sintering at various temperatures to establish the densification threshold. Process the other set using SPS under rapid heating conditions. Compare the temperature at which comparable densification and microstructural quality are achieved.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If SPS does not achieve comparable densification and desired microstructural characteristics at a sintering temperature lower than that required by conventional methods, the hypothesis that SPS reduces sintering temperature is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: According to the traditional alloy design theory, ordered phases or intermetallic compounds will form as the number of alloying elements increases. However, Yeh et al. observes that simple solid solution phases, instead of intermetallic compounds, are formed in an equiatomic quinary alloy. Subsequently, they propose a new alloy system, termed high entropy alloys (HEAs), which contain at least five principal elements, each having the atomic percentage between 5% and 35% [ [1] , [2] ]. Since the development of HEAs, a substantial number of studies on HEA have been performed. Some of these studies are focused on alloys comprised of elements with low melting points, such as AlCoCrCuFeNi system alloys [ [3] , [4] ], commonly exhibiting high ductility and low strength. On the other hand, refractory HEAs have exhibited advantages of high yield strength at room and elevated temperature. Abstract In this study, the wear behaviour of a powder metallurgically produced AlCoCrFeNiTi 0.5 high-entropy alloy (HEAs) is investigated at elevated temperatures. Spark plasma sintering (SPS) of inert gas atomised feedstock enables the production of dense bulk material. The microstructure evolution and phase formation are analysed. The high cooling rate in the atomisation process results in spherical powder with a microstructure comprising two finely distributed body-centred cubic phases. An additional phase with a complex crystal structure precipitates during SPS processing, while no coarsening of microstructural features occurs. The wear resistance under reciprocating wear conditions increases at elevated temperatures due to the formation of a protective oxide layer under atmospherical conditions. Additionally, the coefficient of friction (COF) slightly decreases with increasing temperature. SPS processing is suitable for the production of HEA bulk material. An increase in the wear resistance at elevated temperature enables high temperature applications of the HEA system AlCoCrFeNiTi 0.5 .
